assertion.statement: For the actual elliptic curve E/Q, the Cassels–Tate pairing induces a nondegenerate alternating pairing on the quotient of Sha(E) by its maximal divisible subgroup, hence on its finite2-primary quotient F in the supplied decomposition.
assertion.objects: The canonical principal polarization on E, Sha(E), its maximal divisible subgroup, and F=Sha(E)[2∞]/Sha(E)[2∞]_div.
assertion.hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve over Q. The supplied finite-Selmer/cofinite-generation input gives Sha(E)[2∞]=(Q2/Z2)^t⊕F with F finite. No finiteness of the full Sha group is assumed.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve E/Q; the finite-quotient application holds for its actual2-primary decomposition.
assertion.parameter_range: Canonical genus-one principal polarization;2-primary quotient by maximal divisibility, not the unrestricted pairing on2-torsion.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or uniform finiteness statement.
assertion.constants: The quotient has paired finite primary cyclic factors; in particular dim_F2 F[2] is even.
assertion.normalizations: Cor4 gives c via Pic^(g−1); at g=1 the trivial degree-zero class makes c=0. Cor7 gives alternation. Nondegeneracy is after maximal-divisible quotient. Different primary torsion components are orthogonal.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not equate infinitely divisible elements with the maximal divisible subgroup in an arbitrary group. Current decomposition proves maximality directly. Do not infer nondegeneracy of the restriction to F[2], or finiteSha, or Mordell–Weil rank1 before RC.
assertion.limit_order: First use the separately supplied decomposition and identify its maximal divisible subgroup. Then restrict the quotient pairing to the finite2-primary part and apply the paired-factor argument; only afterward combine with Kummer dimensions.
